As an African American woman, finding a reputable natural hair care salon is a big deal, and I was eager to try their services. Unfortunately, my experience was nothing short of disappointing and left me feeling betrayed and hurt.

On my first visit, the stylist was knowledgeable and seemed passionate about natural hair care. The atmosphere was welcoming, and I left feeling confident about my new style. However, my second visit was a completely different story. The salon had changed, with a new staff and a seemingly new management team. The once warm environment felt cold, and the energy was off.

The nail in the coffin came when I tried their signature curly perm service. The products they used were subpar, and my hair felt dry and damaged after the appointment. The stylist, who seemed inexperienced, struggled to get the color right, and I walked out with a look that was more mess than masterpiece. The smell of the products was overwhelming, and the salon felt unclean, making me question their hygiene standards.

What truly broke the deal was the owner's unresponsive attitude when I brought up my concerns. It felt like they didn't care about my business or my experience, which is unacceptable. For a salon that prides itself on natural hair care, they should know that their clients deserve respect and quality.

I've heard that they don't handle color well on darker skin tones, and I can see why. My color ended up orange, which looked Patchy and unprofessional. It's frustrating as a Black woman to feel like you can't trust a salon to get your color right, especially when you've invested in their services.

The lack of trust and professionalism makes me question why they even call themselves experts in natural hair care. It's a scam, plain and simple. They're preying on the community, offering false promises and delivering subpar results. Don't let them take advantage of us anymore.
